Done
Root cause found — and it is in the harness, not the product
I split dump.txt (313 files, commit 5ebd271), read the register flow end to end, and then read the actual Blazor blazor.web.js source from dotnet/aspnetcore@release/10.0 to confirm it. I did not get to packaging the archive before running out of tool budget, so here is the diagnosis in full — the fix itself is a single file plus one new one, and I can hand you the tar.gz next turn.

What is actually happening
All three failures are the same line — AccountJourneys.cs:149, waiting for button[name='__passkeySubmit'] — reached from RegisterGuestWithPasskeyAsync. That journey is the only one in the harness that navigates by clicking an in-app link instead of page.GotoAsync. Every other journey (CompleteSetupAsync, SignInWithPasskeyAsync, all of AdministrationJourneys, DisplayJourneys.PairAsync) does a real navigation, which is exactly why scenarios 1, 2, 13, 14 and 15 are green and these three are not.

Clicking an in-app link is an enhanced navigation. From NavigationEnhancement.ts, onDocumentClick:

ts
history.pushState(null, '', absoluteInternalHref);   // URL moves FIRST
...
performEnhancedPageLoad(absoluteInternalHref, true); // fetch + synchronizeDomContent AFTER
So the sequence in the failing journey is:

Click Create an account → pushState fires immediately. page.WaitForURLAsync(IsRegistrationUrl) resolves while the sign-in document is still on screen — Playwright resolves a same-document navigation as soon as the URL matches, and there is no load event to wait for.
FillAsync("#username", "e2e.guest") succeeds instantly, because /sign-in also has a #username.
FillAsync("#display-name", …) has to wait — that field only exists on /register. While it waits, the fetch lands and synchronizeDomContent runs. DomSync.ts → ensureEditableValueSynchronized sets destination.value = source.value for every input, and the freshly-rendered register HTML carries value="". The username you just typed is wiped.
Click Continue → posts with Username empty → [Required] fails → OnValidSubmit never fires → step 1 re-renders with "Choose a username."
No __passkeySubmit on screen. 30 s. Timeout. ×3.
It fails deterministically rather than flakily because the fill takes ~2 ms and the fetch ~10–30 ms, so step 2 always wins the race.

Two things this rules out, both of which I chased first: the registration ticket cookie is fine (RegistrationTicketTests already pins the round trip, and /setup proves the identical Secure/Lax/DataProtection cookie mechanic over http://localhost), and /register itself is correct — a real guest clicks the link, watches the page arrive, then types. No product change is warranted. Confirmed from source that form posts are not enhanced by default (enhancedNavigationIsEnabledForForm requires data-enhance on the form itself), so the passkey step and the join POST are ordinary navigations and are not exposed to this.

The fix I'll ship
Two files, both under tests/MyRestaurant.EndToEnd.Tests/:

Harness/EnhancedNavigation.cs (new) — FollowAsync(page, link, arrivalSelector, description, timeout): click, then wait for an element that exists only on the destination surface. Since synchronizeDomContent is one synchronous call, once any part of the patch is visible, all of it is — so that wait turns arrival into a completed fact. Worth its own file because scenario 11 (admin filters the hidden-records view) will click an in-app link too.
Harness/AccountJourneys.cs (full file) — RegisterGuestWithPasskeyAsync uses it with #display-name as the barrier; asserts the URL after arrival rather than waiting on it; reads both fields back with InputValueAsync immediately before submitting and throws a named error if a value was lost; and wraps the __passkeySubmit wait in the diagnostic that was missing, so a failure reports the h1, every p.status-error / .validation-message, and the URL instead of a bare timeout.
Plus docs/_append/BUILD_PROGRESS-m6-slice-8.md and a rewritten _CHANGES.md. Files to delete: docs/llm/vendor/fix_assert_single.py — it is tracked, it did its job, and you've told me you don't want bespoke text-manipulation scripts.

One correction worth stating plainly: slice 5 claimed 6 passed / 9 skipped and slice 6 claimed 8 passed / 7 skipped. Neither was ever observed — scenario 3 has never been green, and 4 and 6 inherited its journey. Expected after this fix: 8 passed / 7 skipped, with dotnet test unchanged at 971 / 0 failed.

I'm deliberately not stacking scenario 5 on top of an unverified harness fix in the same archive — that is precisely the pattern that produced three scenarios reported as passing that never ran. Scenario 5 goes in the slice after this one comes back green.

Say the word and I'll build and hand you m6-slice8-enhanced-nav-fix.tar.gz with full files at exact repo-relative paths.

Done
Root cause found — and it is in the harness, not the product
I split dump.txt (313 files, commit 5ebd271), read the register flow end to end, and then read the actual Blazor blazor.web.js source from dotnet/aspnetcore@release/10.0 to confirm it. I did not get to packaging the archive before running out of tool budget, so here is the diagnosis in full — the fix itself is a single file plus one new one, and I can hand you the tar.gz next turn.

What is actually happening
All three failures are the same line — AccountJourneys.cs:149, waiting for button[name='__passkeySubmit'] — reached from RegisterGuestWithPasskeyAsync. That journey is the only one in the harness that navigates by clicking an in-app link instead of page.GotoAsync. Every other journey (CompleteSetupAsync, SignInWithPasskeyAsync, all of AdministrationJourneys, DisplayJourneys.PairAsync) does a real navigation, which is exactly why scenarios 1, 2, 13, 14 and 15 are green and these three are not.

Clicking an in-app link is an enhanced navigation. From NavigationEnhancement.ts, onDocumentClick:

ts
history.pushState(null, '', absoluteInternalHref);   // URL moves FIRST
...
performEnhancedPageLoad(absoluteInternalHref, true); // fetch + synchronizeDomContent AFTER
So the sequence in the failing journey is:

Click Create an account → pushState fires immediately. page.WaitForURLAsync(IsRegistrationUrl) resolves while the sign-in document is still on screen — Playwright resolves a same-document navigation as soon as the URL matches, and there is no load event to wait for.
FillAsync("#username", "e2e.guest") succeeds instantly, because /sign-in also has a #username.
FillAsync("#display-name", …) has to wait — that field only exists on /register. While it waits, the fetch lands and synchronizeDomContent runs. DomSync.ts → ensureEditableValueSynchronized sets destination.value = source.value for every input, and the freshly-rendered register HTML carries value="". The username you just typed is wiped.
Click Continue → posts with Username empty → [Required] fails → OnValidSubmit never fires → step 1 re-renders with "Choose a username."
No __passkeySubmit on screen. 30 s. Timeout. ×3.
It fails deterministically rather than flakily because the fill takes ~2 ms and the fetch ~10–30 ms, so step 2 always wins the race.

Two things this rules out, both of which I chased first: the registration ticket cookie is fine (RegistrationTicketTests already pins the round trip, and /setup proves the identical Secure/Lax/DataProtection cookie mechanic over http://localhost), and /register itself is correct — a real guest clicks the link, watches the page arrive, then types. No product change is warranted. Confirmed from source that form posts are not enhanced by default (enhancedNavigationIsEnabledForForm requires data-enhance on the form itself), so the passkey step and the join POST are ordinary navigations and are not exposed to this.

The fix I'll ship
Two files, both under tests/MyRestaurant.EndToEnd.Tests/:

Harness/EnhancedNavigation.cs (new) — FollowAsync(page, link, arrivalSelector, description, timeout): click, then wait for an element that exists only on the destination surface. Since synchronizeDomContent is one synchronous call, once any part of the patch is visible, all of it is — so that wait turns arrival into a completed fact. Worth its own file because scenario 11 (admin filters the hidden-records view) will click an in-app link too.
Harness/AccountJourneys.cs (full file) — RegisterGuestWithPasskeyAsync uses it with #display-name as the barrier; asserts the URL after arrival rather than waiting on it; reads both fields back with InputValueAsync immediately before submitting and throws a named error if a value was lost; and wraps the __passkeySubmit wait in the diagnostic that was missing, so a failure reports the h1, every p.status-error / .validation-message, and the URL instead of a bare timeout.
Plus docs/_append/BUILD_PROGRESS-m6-slice-8.md and a rewritten _CHANGES.md. Files to delete: docs/llm/vendor/fix_assert_single.py — it is tracked, it did its job, and you've told me you don't want bespoke text-manipulation scripts.

One correction worth stating plainly: slice 5 claimed 6 passed / 9 skipped and slice 6 claimed 8 passed / 7 skipped. Neither was ever observed — scenario 3 has never been green, and 4 and 6 inherited its journey. Expected after this fix: 8 passed / 7 skipped, with dotnet test unchanged at 971 / 0 failed.

I'm deliberately not stacking scenario 5 on top of an unverified harness fix in the same archive — that is precisely the pattern that produced three scenarios reported as passing that never ran. Scenario 5 goes in the slice after this one comes back green.

Say the word and I'll build and hand you m6-slice8-enhanced-nav-fix.tar.gz with full files at exact repo-relative paths.

No src/ file changes. /register is correct — a real guest clicks the link, watches the page arrive, then types. The harness was the thing reading an address bar that Blazor moves before it moves the page: history.pushState fires on the link click, the fetch and synchronizeDomContent come after, WaitForURLAsync returns while the sign-in document is still up, #username gets typed into the wrong page, and the DOM patch then resets every input to what the server rendered. Empty username, [Required] fails, no credential step, thirty-second timeout on a button three states away from the cause.
